column10: This mask is great for blackheads and clogged pores, and as a spot treatment for large pimples. It works best when used right after a shower, in my experience steaming for only a short time does not let it work to its full potential. This is a clay mask, not a peel off mask. This means it draws sebum/dead skin to the surface of your skin, but they do not actually stick to the mask. You should either perform very gentle extractions (hardly even extracting, since the dirt has already been drawn out of the pore) or use an AHA or BHA product to dissolve the dirt after using the mask. Also do NOT let the mask dry out until it starts to get cracked and itchy, this is too long and draws too much moisture out of your skin and will irritate it. (However you can do this if you are trying to dry out a large pimple and do it on a very small area.) ALWAYS follow with a moisturizer. One more tip: even though it takes longer, it is better to gently rinse off this mask with your fingers than scrub it off; scrubbing will further irritate your skin.

column10: I just bought my second tube of Origins Clear Improvement Active Charcoal Mask after using the mask regularly for the past 8 weeks. I?ôve found there are a few tricks to getting results with this mask after my first couple of experiences with it were less than stellar.1. This is not your typical clay or mud mask. Charcoal works differently on the skin and I?ôve found it essential to have a pre-mask ritual, which consists of opening my pores in one way or another. I usually use the mask after a bath or a warm shower so my skin is flushed and moist and my pores are open. Otherwise, a hot compress applied directly to the face for a minute or two will open the pores and prep the skin for this mask (and it feels great). I found that when I didn?ôt prep my skin this way the results were disastrous: the mask pulled at my skin, was nearly impossible to scrub off, left me with red and blotchy skin from the effort and did not appear to clear away any dead skin or black heads clogging my pores.2. After opening the pores quickly (so the skin is still warm and the pores are still open when the mask is applied) work a gentle exfoliant over the skin and rinse off in warm/tepid water. The exfoliating action of a wet washcloth might be enough, depending on the sensitivity level of your skin. I alternate between a washcloth and a gentle face scrub with micro beads.3. Apply a THIN layer of the mask. I normally pile on a mud or clay mask but it took upwards of 4 (!) washes with my strongest, heavily foaming face wash to remove the charcoal mask when I applied it thick. A good rule of thumb is to apply it so that there are no streaks or transparent patches but not so thick as to have a ridge forming where skin meets mask. It is not a peel off mask.4. Let it sit until just barely dried. When it no longer comes off onto the fingers after a gentle pat across the face then it?ôs about time to wash it off. I waited 15-20 minutes the first few times I used it (thinking the longer it was on the more work it would do) and that was a huge mistake. The longer it sits dry on the skin, the harder it was to remove and the more red, sensitive, itchy and blotchy my skin was after. Plus, having it sit so long as to pull and tug at the skin as it (over)dries is uncomfortable. There is no recommended drying time on the tube but for me in a relatively dry climate, I leave it for about 7-10 minutes.5. Even following the steps above doesn?ôt make it a particularly easy mask to remove. It takes me two rinses with an otherwise effective, foaming face wash, really working it into the mask before turning on the faucet and rinsing it off. A washcloth actually works better. You can get all of the mask in one go with a wet cloth and the skin is so squeaky clean after there is no need to follow with a cleanser.Blackhead removal is super easy after all of the steps above, which is a plus. The mask doesn?ôt seem to actually pull the blackheads out though the way a pore strip or some of the peel off masks claim to do. My regular use of the mask (2-3 times a week, which is more than recommended) has made my skin drier than it used to be so I am backing off to only once or twice a week (I like a good cleansing mask, what can I say). I like the immediate appearance of clarity that it gives my complexion so I highly recommend giving it a try!

column10: I do microneedling & I have all my patients use this for after care. It?ôs phenomenal! However I think some of the reviewers on here my not be using it correctly. This product is hydrophilic meaning it loves water. It uses that water to penetrate into your skin and give your skin that plump look. Therefore this product needs to be used with damp skin. If you dry your face thoroughly & then apply it, it will not have water to help it absorb into your skin. So it will sit on top of your skin and cause piling. Also once the product absorbs all the water underneath your skin it will help with tightening and plumping and in order to seal in that plumpness you need a good moisturizer to seal it in. So first wash face with a damp skin then apply this product, once dry and absorbed add your moisturizer and then add a mineral sunscreen over the moisturizer. Hope this helps anyone who is starting their adventure with HA products :)

They will damage your skin and can actually make acne worse). After trying several different expensive moisturizers whose fragrance irritated my tired skin, I discovered The Ordinary. I am super cautious to claim that any one product can fix your skin, because let?ôs face it, that is an advertising ploy meant to lure you into buying more unnecessary products. BUT! There is reason this is used in so many face care products as a featured ingredient. Hyaluronic acid is a naturally occurring substance in the skin that draws and locks in moisture from the environment. Unfortunately your skin produces less as you age. Many derma fillers are made using hyaluronic acid to help smooth fine lines and wrinkles. Syrums like this use molecules too large to really sink into the skin and rather sit on top as a surface barrier (still very important!) If you live in a dry environment, this may not be super effective, as there is no moisture to draw in to the skin and instead, it may draw moisture out of the deep layers of the skin. This can be helped by using other acids in your evening routine that target the deeper layers of your skin. I also highly suggest pairing this with a thicker moisturizer on top, as this is meant to mimic your skin?ôs water barrier. You only need a small amount of this to spread a thin layer over the skin. If you find that it pills when adding other products on top, trying waiting a few minutes for it to dry.
